title: Metric descent and rank-preserving contractions
main_claim: Theorem 2.1 (toroidal volume metric): given a smooth semipositive metric on -K_X, an equidimensional toroidal model and generic adjoint rank one at exponent zero, -K_Y+A_0 carries an unweighted integrable semipositive metric, where A_0 is an explicit correction whose pullback is p-exceptional. Theorem 4.1 (rank-preserving contraction): if X has no forms, -K_X is smoothly semipositive, a torus T acts, and the generic invariant section and adjoint-rank-one conditions hold, then either H^0(X,-rK_X)^T≠0 or the fibration factors through a lower-dimensional base that keeps both conditions. Corollaries: allowed-pole nonvanishing (Thm g:allowed) and H^0(V,-mK_V)^T≠0 (Thm rb:invariant).

issues.description: Campana–Păun's orbifold cotangent theorem is applied to the pair (Z,Δ_t), whose boundary coefficients are arbitrary rationals 1-c_i in [0,1) plus 1/N. The step that justifies the adapted-cover inclusion τ^*Ω_Z ⊂ E_t uses the generator w^{-bγ}dz without saying that the branching order b must make bγ integral, or that a rounding is taken. This is a presentation gap. The inclusion and the determinant identity c_1(E_t)=τ^*(K_Z+Δ_t) are standard for rational orbifold multiplicities, so the conclusion is not affected.
issues.evidence: "at a branch z=w^b corresponding to boundary coefficient γ, the orbifold generator is w^{-bγ}dz; hence the ordinary generator dz belongs to the adapted bundle"

coverage: I read the introduction and these sections in full: toroidal-volume (Thm 2.1, Lemma g:volume-subklt, Cor g:correction-iitaka-zero), analytic-input (transfer lemma, rank-one moments lemma, determinant lemma), contraction (whole proof of Thm g:cf:contraction-theorem), reductions (all three proofs of allowed-pole nonvanishing), the start of boundary-transfer (weighted approximation, slope principle, finite-volume cotangent estimate), and the rank-one proof of rb:invariant in orbit-integrals. I re-derived by hand: the coefficient bound -a_E+e_E a_Q ≤ 1-e_E; the sub-klt argument via B=D_W-Θ; the pushforward exponent (1+a)/e-1; the extension upper bounds for Φ and φ_M; the residual exponents in the logarithmic coarea upper bound; the zero-Lelong lower bound and nefness via Nadel and Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity; the identity K_Z+Δ_t ~ B^-+tA; the three-index linear equivalence and the affine-slope argument; the pole control off G; the zero β-degree of h_*ĝ^*A_W; the Harder–Narasimhan argument in the slope principle; and the pushdown in the Druel/Ou step. I did not read in detail the later variant sections (fields, boundary-applications, multiplicative-systems, reduced-flat), the remainder of boundary-transfer, or the Prékopa/Brascamp–Lieb second proof.
sibling_notes: The family 068 board had one entry: Bounded-anticanonical-metrics-on-klt-pairs-and-torus-quotients (rank 6, no_gap_found). It uses the same determinant and Hard Lefschetz and torus-orbit machinery. That matches what I found here: the determinant lemma (DPS hard Lefschetz plus the Lazić–Peternell determinant) checks. It did not change the assessment. This paper cites the companion HFiniteVolume for alternative proofs only and does not depend on it, so there is no circularity.
